report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of wiki/vault.py: functions discover_vaults and page_tree, constant PROJECT_VAULT_DIR. Claims in docstrings and comments checked.

handoff.purpose: Contains discover_vaults, page_tree, and constant PROJECT_VAULT_DIR.

symbols.name: PROJECT_VAULT_DIR
symbols.note: String 'docs/wiki' indicating where a project vault lives.

symbols.name: discover_vaults
symbols.note: Returns list of Vault objects from repo_root and optional global_root.

symbols.name: page_tree
symbols.note: Returns nested dict tree from list of page objects, sorted by name.

claims.text: Where a project vault lives. One place, so a page's address is stable.
claims.why: The comment asserts stability but the chunk does not define 'page's address' or prove uniqueness.

claims.text: The vaults visible from a project, project first.
claims.why: The function adds project vault first (if exists), then global vault; order matches 'project first'.

claims.text: The global vault is OPT-IN via an explicit argument rather than a default home-directory path: it lives outside the repo, and everything outside the repo root breaks assumptions the index, the write-confinement rules and the egress lane all make. Until those are answered it must be a deliberate act.
claims.why: The function only adds global vault if global_root argument is provided and non-None; no default path is used.

claims.text: Nested tree from page paths. Deterministic: every level sorted by name.
claims.why: The function sorts pages by rel, and norm function sorts directory keys by name; tree is deterministic.

observations.what: PROJECT_VAULT_DIR is a constant string but not used inside this chunk (used externally).
discover_vaults uses repo_root.resolve().name for project vault name; might be misleading if repo_root is not canonical.
page_tree sorts pages by p.rel, but the sorting key lambda is redundant (sorted already does lexicographic).
